description:
A nuclear detonation is survivable — even without a bunker. But your instincts will kill you faster than the radiation. The physics of nuclear survival follow a strict 72-hour protocol: if you understand blast dynamics, improvised shielding, and the mathematical Rule of Sevens for radiation decay, you can ride out the deadliest hours in human history inside your own home.

In this video, Fallout Guy breaks down the complete step-by-step nuclear survival protocol from the moment of detonation through the critical 72-hour shelter period. We cover why the flash blinds you permanently and how to survive the overpressure shockwave, the 15-minute fallout window you must use to reach dense shelter, how to build improvised radiation shielding using halving thickness with mattresses, dirt, books, and water containers, the decontamination wash-down procedure including why hair conditioner is lethal after nuclear fallout, the truth about potassium iodide pills and the liquid iodine skin-absorption alternative, the hydration paradox — how to harvest 40-50 gallons of safe uncontaminated water already trapped inside your home without ever leaving your shield, and the Rule of Sevens that mathematically guarantees radiation decays to survivable levels within 72 hours.

Topics Covered: — How to survive a nuclear strike without a bunker — The overpressure shockwave and why you keep your mouth open — The glass fragmentation kill zone and where to shelter immediately — The 15-minute fallout window for reaching dense shelter — Improvised radiation shielding using halving thickness — Nuclear decontamination: why conditioner binds radioactive isotopes — Potassium iodide vs liquid iodine tincture for thyroid protection — The hydration paradox: harvesting water from your hot water heater and pipes — The Rule of Sevens: radiation decay math that saves your life — The 72-hour nuclear survival timeline from flash to evacuation

FALLOUT WARDEN — What to do when normal stops working. Subscribe and enable notifications. When the grid goes down, you won't have time to search for answers.
